  MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, December 6, 2021

1.  The City Council Meeting was opened to the public and the Council Chambers was opened.  In an effort to keep
  a safe environment and to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, the City limited occupancy and required
  masking for those in attendance. To facilitate public participation for those who did not wish to attend in person,
  the meeting was made available virtually.

2.  At 6: 30 p. m., Mayor Hepburn kicked off the holiday season by lighting the City' s Christmas tree along with the
  Bonita Migh School Choir who sang holiday songs until Santa Claus appeared to take pictures with the children.
3.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6:55 p. m.
4.  Council Members present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Principal Planner Candice Bowcock

5.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Hepburn.

  Community Events  announced that the Historical Society is fundraising to restore Inman Conety' s

9.  Active Transportation Plan  Principal Planner Bowcock reported on the Active Transportation Plan. She
  stated that the Active Transportation Plan establishes the City' s vision and
  comprehensive approach to improving walking, biking, and rolling in La Verne.

  The Plan strives to improve facilities, such as sidewalks and bike lanes to
  enhance access to and experiences of active transportation and provide more
  opportunities for local, recreational movement, inclusive of any age or ability.

  She informed the City Council that Consultant Matt Braughton from Kittelson &
  Association was available to answer any questions that Council may have.
  Staff, Planning Commission, and the Active Transportation Committee
  recommended that the City Council approve the proposed Active
  Transportation Plan.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There were several public comments at the meeting. ( To hear what was said
  during public comment, please visit the City's website to view the archived
  Council meeting.)

  The City Council discussed the Active Transportation Plan and thanked
  Principal Planner Bowcock and staff for their work on prepari ng a great plan.

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried to
  approve Resolution No. 21- 91 , adopting the Active Transportation Plan.

13.  Mayor Hepburn adjourned the Council meeting at 8:54 in memory of Catherine Fugitt, who died on October 15,
  2021 at the age of 98. She was a long-time La Verne resident and contributed nearly 50 years as a community
  activist. In 1945, she volunteered in relief and education efforts for Japanese children and families and helped
  restructure Japanese school systems. Her work in Japan marked the beginning of her tendency to expand
  awareness and tolerance to choose diverse people to learn and love. Catherine and her husband Jay were the
  co-founders of La Verne's Friends of the Library. They persuaded La Verne citizens and Los Angeles County
  Supervisors to support a library for La Verne, and raised$  50, 000 to help build it. Catherine also was active in the
  La Verne Senior and Community Center, 210 Freeway Extension, La Verne Fire and Paramedic Program, and
  the development of Edwards Theatre. Catherine and her husband Jay were the first recipients of the Pride of La
  Verne Award in 1993 and both received the Los Angeles County Library System Citizen of the Year Award.
  Catherine's legacy lives on in the hearts of all who Verne".
  knew her. Former Councilmember Tom Harvey was quoted
  saying that Catherine was" one
  of the hearts of La  Catherine is survived by a large extended family
  including numerous" chosen" children; and

  In memory of Delia Heredia a long-time La Verne resident and downtown La Verne business owner who died on
  November 14, 2021.  Delia was born in Culiacan Sinaloa, Mexico to a large family. She was the lucky number
  seven of 11 children. At the age of 16, she left her hometown and worked as a teller in Tijuana, Mexico to pay for
  cosmetology school. She immigrated to the United States in 1989 and earned her cosmetology license. She
  worked in different salons in Ontario and Pomona until she opened her own business in La Verne, Delia' s
  Barbershop in 1999. She felt very fortunate to have found a nice store in a nice town. On top of running a
  business and being a single parent, Qelia participated in her community church' s activities, participated in local
  events like the La Verne Wine Walk and she was secretary and treasurer of the Old Town La Verne Business
  Improvement District Advisory Board. Delia also traveled to people's homes that were not able to leave their
  home due to disabilities to give them a haircut. Delia valued family, hard work, education, and perseverance.
  Everyone she met stated that her smile truly brightened everyone around her and she al vays had kind words.
  She is survived by three daughters and her
  granddaughter.

Honorable Mayor and Council,

It has come to my attention of the Mayor' s attempt to eliminate the City of La Verne' s
retirement gift given  in recognition of years of service an employee has given. I' m surprised by

the pettiness of this council to even consider doing away with this benefit.

Per the Employee Recognition Program employees retiring with 5 years or more of service
receive a gift  ranging from$ 250 to$ 2, 500 depending on years of service. This  ranges from 5
years up to 30 years or more. Depending on length of time employee works, the average annual
cost to  city ranges from$ 25 to$ 83 per year. This is a minimal price for the city to show their
appreciation to the employee.

I have witnessed a few retirements during my 40+ years with the city. I have seen the city use

that money for luncheons  and/ or gifts  for the retiring employee. While we are not talking a

large amount of money, it is none the less exciting watching the employee receive a gift that

pertains to his/ her hobby or for a project that the employee intends to work on in retirement.
Be it  a  fishing pole and  rod,  barbecue  grill  for  outdoor  kitchen, inflatable tube,  etc.  the

employee is always very happy with the gift they receive and the appreciation the city shows in
giving it. A retirement is probably the greatest opportunity for the city to show how much they
appreciated the years of dedicated service the employee gave you.

The council, including you Mr. Mayor, are always stating how much they appreciate all the hard
work the employees do on a daily basis, especially during this Covid pandemic. Yet, your actions
appear to state otherwise. Taking away this perk which is not a major expense shows that you
don' t appreciate your long term employees despite what you claim.

With a growing turnover rate in the city, those who stay and provide years of service should be
rewarded with a small token of appreciation from the city. It is my hope that you will reconsider
and vote to continue with the retirement gift for employees who have provided great service to
the City of La Verne.

Sincerely,

Richard J. Martinez
Utillities Manager

Honorable Mayor and City Council,

On behalf of all the members of la Verne City Employee Association ( CEA), I would like to
  regarding the possible dissolution of the City of La Verne
  retirement " gifts"
express concern

that have been given to City of La Verne retirees for decades now. The request for this item to
be placed on the agenda by our Mayor, is surprising. Members of the CEA group would assume
that we have consistent support from our mayor for years of loyal service.

The message our CEA group will interpret from this discussion is that long term, dedicated
employees are not valued in the City of La Verne. Currently, a 10 year employee could receive
between $ 250-$ 500 towards a retirement lunch or gift. That is a mere$ 25 to$ 50 per year of
service as a " Thank you." A 30 year employee could receive up to $2500 towards their

retirement lunch or gift that is$  83 per year. Bottom line that is not a lot of money for ten to
thirty years of DEDICATED SERVICE!!!

Our members have a work week that consists of 36 hours per week, which was voted in many
years ago. This saves the city 10% of hourly expenses, but results in lower annual income and

contribution  to each member' s retirement.  To present the dissolution of retirement gifts,
which does not seem to save a monumental amount of money for the City, needs to be
withdrawn. This may tarnish the perception of appreciation many members of the CEA group
thought we all had from our Mayor and Council.

Mr. Mayor I ask you, since you want to review employees " gifts," instead look into paying each
member of the CEA group a 40 hour work week. (  This will reflect the support that this usually

quiet group would definitely appreciate.)

I am concerned that if this is approved, the interpretation by the CEA group will simply be that
loyal long term employees are not appreciated by our Mayor and Council. It is to be expected
that the large turnover of employees will continue.

Again this is a slap in the face for those of us who serve the community of la Verne and have
done so for many of years.

Sincerely,

Janelle Gray
CEA union President
